title: Nested double-tier escalation: URL import runs two independent tier waterfalls that can each end in a Gemini call (up to 3 LLM calls per failed import)
evidence: url_import_strategy.dart:113-115 (Tier 1) and :133-138 (Tier 3, re-run on scraper HTML) call RecipeParserService.parseFromUrl with no useLlm override; recipe_parser_service.dart:250-255 shows useLlm defaults to true and :443 shows LlmTier runs unless useLlm=false. So the inner 4-tier waterfall (SchemaOrg→SiteConfig→RuleBased→LlmTier) can invoke Gemini once on HTTP HTML and again on WebScraper HTML, and if both fail the outer waterfall reaches its OWN LLM fallback at Tier 6 (url_import_strategy.dart:169-180, LlmExtractionFallback). The two systems also duplicate each other's non-LLM tiers: inner SchemaOrgTier vs outer _tryStructuredExtraction (url_import_strategy.dart:117-124, both JSON-LD extraction back-to-back on the same HTML), and inner SiteConfigTier (Firestore site_configs, seed-site-configs.ts:92-96, selector 'h1.recipe-header__title') vs outer SiteParserRegistry Dart parsers (ica_recipe_parser.dart:99-106, different selector guesses for the same domains). Ownership of escalation is split across two files with no single tier ledger; _logImportEvent records the outer tier only.
recommendation: Make RecipeParserService the single tier owner: pass useLlm:false from _tryEnhancedParser and keep exactly one LLM escalation point (or delete LlmExtractionFallback and let LlmTier be it). Fold the outer structured-extraction/site-parser tiers into the inner service as tiers, or explicitly document which system wins per stage; reconcile the two per-site selector configs (Firestore site_configs vs SiteParserRegistry) into one source.

verdict.evidence: Read the cited files; the double-tier escalation is real. (1) url_import_strategy.dart:114 (Tier 1, HTTP HTML) and :133-137 (Tier 3, scraper HTML) both call _tryEnhancedParser, which at :212-215 calls parser.parseFromUrl(url:, htmlContent:) with NO useLlm argument. (2) recipe_parser_service.dart:255 shows useLlm defaults to true; :443 skips LlmTier only when useLlm=false; :198-207 confirms LlmTier is registered as the 4th inner tier; llm_tier.dart:60-67 shows shouldSkip only guards empty content / null LLM service — no other gate. So a hard-to-parse page can trigger a Gemini call on HTTP HTML (inner LlmTier), again on scraper HTML (inner LlmTier re-run), and if both parseFromUrl calls fail, the outer waterfall's own LLM fallback fires at url_import_strategy.dart:169-180 (_llmFallback.tryExtraction) — up to 3 full LLM extraction calls per failed import (potentially more: _trySelectiveIngredientEnhancement at recipe_parser_service.dart:479-486 makes an additional smaller LLM call before each LlmTier run). Duplication claims also hold: outer _tryStructuredExtraction (url_import_strategy.dart:119, :140-143) runs JSON-LD extraction on the same HTML the inner SchemaOrgTier just processed, and _logImportEvent at :121/:145/:177 records only outer tier names, so the inner tier that actually fired is not in the outer ledger. Nothing in .claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md covers import-waterfall LLM escalation. Minor note: 3 LLM calls is the worst case for a page whose LLM extractions fail or score below threshold; when the first LlmTier call succeeds, only 1 call occurs — but the finding's cost/ownership claim is accurate as stated.

title: Household/present-diner allergen filtering is dead code in every menu-generation path — generation always uses single-user filtering
evidence: getAvailableRecipesAsync() (menu_generator.dart:106, the only method honoring presentMemberIds and useHouseholdAllergens) has ZERO callers anywhere in lib/ (grep). generateMenuFromPrompt (:321,:325), regenerateMenuSection (:470), and swapSingleRecipe (:507) all read the sync availableRecipes getter (:91-103), which only applies single-user prefs. useHouseholdAllergens is exposed via a MenuViewModel setter (menu_viewmodel.dart:112-114) that no view calls; presentMemberIds on MenuGenerator (:70) is set by nothing. So even when the deferred present-set UI ships, wiring the flag would still be inert because the generation entry points are hardwired to the sync getter. Two parallel pool getters exist and generation is bound to the unsafe one.
recommendation: Make generateMenuFromPrompt/regenerateMenuSection/swapSingleRecipe await getAvailableRecipesAsync() (it already falls back to single-user filtering when no household exists), delete the sync getter from the generation path, and add a test asserting the household path is exercised by generateMenuFromPrompt. If the feature is deliberately deferred, delete or clearly gate the dead fields so the memory/docs claim of 'present-aware filtering built' can't be mistaken for 'wired'.

verdict.evidence: menu_generator.dart: getAvailableRecipesAsync() (line 106) is the only method honoring presentMemberIds (:116-130) and useHouseholdAllergens (:132-144), but grep shows its only callers are in test/unit/viewmodels/menu/menu_generator_present_aware_test.dart — zero callers in lib/. All generation entry points read the sync `availableRecipes` getter (:91-103, single-user filtering only): generateMenuFromPrompt (:321, :325), regenerateMenuSection (:470), swapSingleRecipe (:507), plus :299 and :618. `useHouseholdAllergens` is only touched by the MenuViewModel getter/setter (menu_viewmodel.dart:112-114), which no view calls; `presentMemberIds` on MenuGenerator (:70) is assigned nowhere in lib/ (the family_rating_entry hits are a different class). So even if the deferred present-set UI set the flags, generation would still use the single-user pool. Not listed in accepted-deviations.md. Nuance: project memory records present-aware filtering as deliberately deferred generator-side capability pending the per-night UI, so this is a known-deferred wiring gap rather than a regression — but the finding's core claim (entry points hardwired to the sync getter, so wiring the flags would be inert) is accurate.

title: OS share-sheet import runs a parallel, degraded extraction pipeline that bypasses the entire import architecture
evidence: receive_share_view.dart:159 calls SocialMediaExtractor.extractFromUrl → ExtractionManager → WebScraper JS text scrape, then routes raw text to the '/franSocialaMedier' text-import screen (:174-181). This bypasses ImportManager entirely: no YouTubeImportStrategy transcript extraction, no Instagram/TikTok 4-tier pipelines, no 7-tier URL waterfall, no GlobalRecipeCache, no ImportRateLimiter, no ParseEventLogger telemetry. web_scraper.dart:257-267: YouTube and Pinterest (both enumerated as supported in platform_detector.dart:32-33) fall to the default extractGeneric body scrape — for YouTube the recipe lives in the description/transcript, so this near-always fails silently into 'no content'. A schema.org-perfect recipe site shared via share sheet is degraded from structured JSON-LD extraction to body-text heuristics. Path A has zero learning-loop/telemetry hooks, so its failure rate is invisible.
recommendation: Route the share-sheet URL into ImportManager.autoImport (which already handles platform dispatch, tiers, cache, rate limits, and telemetry) and retire ExtractionManager/PlatformDetector as a separate URL pipeline; keep WebScraper as shared plumbing only.

verdict.evidence: Core structural claim CONFIRMED: the share-sheet flow never reaches ImportManager.autoImport. receive_share_view.dart:159 calls SocialMediaExtractor.extractFromUrl (WebView scrape) and routes raw text to '/franSocialaMedier' (:174-181); import_manager.dart:38-113 confirms autoImport owns GlobalRecipeCache, YouTubeImportStrategy, TikTokPipeline, InstagramPipeline, ImportRateLimiter — none touched by the share path. So Instagram/TikTok shares get the WebView extractor (web_scraper.dart:257-263) instead of the 4-tier pipelines, and no cache/rate-limit applies. Several evidence details are wrong, though: (1) YouTube shares do NOT hit the SocialMediaExtractor path — content_detector_service.dart:268-281 classifies only instagram/facebook/tiktok as socialMediaUrl; YouTube falls to ContentType.recipeUrl and routes to '/importViaUrl' (receive_share_view.dart:131-137). The degradation is still real (url_import_viewmodel.dart:315-341 uses WebScraper; PlatformDetector→youtube→default extractGeneric at web_scraper.dart:266-267, no transcript strategy) but via a different route. (2) A schema.org recipe site shared via share sheet also goes to '/importViaUrl', where whitelisted domains (ICA, Arla, köket, allrecipes etc., platform_detector.dart:57-79) get real JSON-LD extraction via RecipeSiteContentExtractor (recipe_site_content_extractor.dart:19-21); only non-whitelisted schema.org sites degrade to extractGeneric. (3) "Zero telemetry" is overstated: receive_share_view logs import-funnel analytics (logImportStarted :98, logImportSuccess :166, logExtractionError :187) and the final text parse still runs through ImportManager's text strategy (import_base_viewmodel.dart:80). What's true is no ParseEventLogger URL-tier telemetry, no cache, no rate limiting. (4) The degraded pipeline is not share-sheet-specific — the manual '/importViaUrl' screen shares it; only the primary "Importera länk" tile (lagg_till_recept_view.dart:154 → /smartImport → smart_import_viewmodel.dart:293 autoImport) uses the full pipeline. Not covered by accepted-deviations.md.
verdict.correctedDetail: Two parallel URL import pipelines exist: SmartImport ('/smartImport' → ImportManager.autoImport with platform pipelines, YouTube transcripts, cache, rate limiter, telemetry) vs the legacy WebScraper pipeline used by BOTH the OS share sheet and the manual '/importViaUrl' screen. Share-sheet corrections: YouTube/Pinterest shares route via ContentType.recipeUrl to '/importViaUrl' (not the social-media text extract), still ending in a generic body scrape with no transcript extraction; whitelisted recipe domains (ICA, Arla, köket, allrecipes, etc.) DO get JSON-LD extraction in this pipeline — only non-whitelisted schema.org sites degrade to body-text heuristics; the path has funnel analytics (logImportStarted/Success/ExtractionError) and the final text parse uses ImportManager's text strategy, but lacks ParseEventLogger URL-tier telemetry, GlobalRecipeCache, and ImportRateLimiter. Recommendation stands: route share-sheet (and '/importViaUrl') URLs into ImportManager.autoImport.

title: Correction-driven alias learning auto-mutates live ingredient master data (allergen-relevant) at 3 users with no review or revert path
evidence: analyze-corrections.ts:29 ALIAS_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD = 3; :273-283 — once 3 distinct users' corrections agree, arrayUnion writes learnedAliasesSv onto the production ingredients/{id} doc with no human review gate and no demotion path. findIngredientByName (:94-97) only verifies the target ingredient exists, not that the mapping is sane. The ingredient lookup that consumes learnedAliasesSv drives Phase-1 allergen tri-state tagging, so a poisoned or shared-typo alias (3 users mis-correcting the same OCR artifact) can remap an allergen-bearing ingredient name onto an allergen-free ingredient and silently flip a recipe's allergen status app-wide. Corrections originate from the client-writable parsing_corrections collection (firestore.rules:2005), so the 3-user quorum is the only integrity control.
recommendation: Add a review step (admin-dashboard approve queue, or at minimum a hold for aliases touching any allergen-property ingredient), a revert/blocklist mechanism, and an audit log entry per auto-approval. Raise the threshold or require the alias to survive N days without conflicting corrections.

verdict.evidence: Read functions/src/analytics/analyze-corrections.ts in full. Confirmed: ALIAS_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD = 3 (line 29); processAliasCandidate (lines 256-291) auto-approves inside a transaction once 3 distinct userIds accumulate and writes the alias straight onto the production master doc via tx.update(ingredients/{id}, learnedAliasesSv arrayUnion) (lines 279-283) — no human review gate. The only integrity check is findIngredientByName on the CORRECTED name (lines 241-247), which verifies the target exists, not that the original→target mapping is sane; the original name is never checked (it can even shadow an existing ingredient's canonical name). There is no demotion/revert/blocklist path anywhere in the file — status only goes pending→approved; getCorrectionStats (lines 311-364) is a read-only admin view, not an approval queue. Corrections are client-creatable: firestore.rules ~line 2014 allows any authenticated user to create parsing_corrections docs for themselves (immutable, but creation is the attack/typo vector), so the 3-user quorum is indeed the sole control. Downstream impact confirmed: lib/repositories/firebase/firebase_ingredient_repository.dart:226-231 indexes learnedAliasesSv into _aliasIndex, the lookup that drives ingredient matching for tagging/allergen classification, so a wrong alias remaps names app-wide (and lib/models/tagging/ingredient_data.dart:378 includes them in allAliases). Checked .claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md — nothing covers this pattern. One softening note (not a refutation): at current ~1-user pre-launch scale, assembling 3 distinct authenticated users is a real but low-likelihood collusion bar; the shared-OCR-typo scenario at scale is the credible path.

title: Household/present-diner allergen filtering is dead code in production menu generation — and its tests call the dead method directly, staying green while the safety feature never fires
evidence: Repo-wide grep: `getAvailableRecipesAsync` has ZERO callers in lib/ beyond its own definition (lib/viewmodels/menu/menu_generator.dart:106). All three production generation paths use the sync `availableRecipes` getter, which only does single-user filtering: generateMenuFromPrompt at menu_generator.dart:321/325, regenerateMenuSection at :470, swap at :507/:618. The `useHouseholdAllergens` toggle is exposed to the UI (lib/viewmodels/menu_viewmodel.dart:112-114) but is only read inside the never-called async method (menu_generator.dart:132), so the user-visible switch is inert. `presentMemberIds` (menu_generator.dart:70) is never set from any production code (the family-viewmodel presentMemberIds hits are an unrelated field). Meanwhile every test in menu_generator_present_aware_test.dart invokes `generator.getAvailableRecipesAsync()` directly (lines 138, 156, 181, 198, 227) — the tests prove the dead method's internal logic but nothing asserts that generateMenuFromPrompt's recipe pool respects household or present-diner allergens, so this whole suite stays green under the real user-facing bug: a family with a child's allergen registered still gets menus containing that allergen when the household toggle is on.
recommendation: Wire the async path in: make generateMenuFromPrompt/regenerateMenuSection/swapSingleRecipe await getAvailableRecipesAsync() (or fold household/present logic into pool construction), then add a behavioral test at the generateMenuFromPrompt level: household with allergen X + filterByAllergens + useHouseholdAllergens=true → generated menu contains no recipe with allergenStatus[X]==contains. Keep the existing tests but re-anchor at least one on the public generation entry point so a future unwiring fails a test.

verdict.evidence: Grep across lib/ shows `getAvailableRecipesAsync` is defined at lib/viewmodels/menu/menu_generator.dart:106 and has ZERO production callers; all generation paths use the sync `availableRecipes` getter (menu_generator.dart:91-103, used at :321/:325/:470/:507/:618), which only applies single-user `_filterByAllergenPreferences`/`_filterByDietaryPreferences`. Household aggregation (:132-144) and present-diner filtering (:116-130) live only inside the uncalled async method. `useHouseholdAllergens` is set only via menu_viewmodel.dart:113-114 and read only at menu_generator.dart:132 — so even if set, it does nothing. `presentMemberIds` on the generator (:70) is never assigned anywhere in lib/ (the family_rating_entry_viewmodel hits are a different class's field). All five tests in test/unit/viewmodels/menu/menu_generator_present_aware_test.dart (lines 138, 156, 181, 198, 227) call `generator.getAvailableRecipesAsync()` directly, none exercise `generateMenuFromPrompt`, so the suite stays green while the feature never fires in production. Not in accepted-deviations.md. Two nuances that don't change the verdict: (1) no widget binds `useHouseholdAllergens` (grep outside lib/ = 0 hits), so the toggle is VM-exposed but not actually rendered in any UI — "user-visible switch is inert" overstates slightly; (2) project memory notes the present-set UI driving `presentMemberIds` was a known deferred step, but the household-union path being unwired from generation is not a recorded deferral.

title: The 3,300-line tag_generator_test.dart pins a dead orchestrator — TagGenerator.generate() has zero production callers; live tagging runs through TaggingPipelineRunner with different timeout/partial semantics
evidence: Grep over lib/ finds no call to `.generate(` on TagGenerator anywhere; production (lib/services/tagging/tagging_pipeline_runner.dart:130-140, 326) calls runPhase1..runPhase5 + assembleResult. Yet tag_generator_test.dart contains 250+ invocations of `generator.generate(...)` (lines 27 through 3330), including an entire block of C3/HIGH-7 timeout-and-skip orchestration tests — semantics implemented only inside the dead generate() method (tag_generator.dart:165-260: stopwatch-based check-after-each-phase, skip-ALL-on-timeout), which differ from the live runner's per-phase Future.timeout budgets. The phase calculators exercised through generate() are real, so the file isn't worthless, but its orchestration assertions (timeout behavior, phase-skip asymmetry, isPartial bookkeeping) verify unreachable code and give false confidence: a regression in TaggingPipelineRunner's assembly/partial logic would not fail this giant suite, and conversely this suite blocks deleting the dead method.
recommendation: Delete TagGenerator.generate() (project rule: root-cause cleanup over annotation). Re-home the phase-behavior tests onto direct phase-calculator calls or the pipeline runner (the correct seam already demonstrated by tagging_pipeline_runner_test.dart), and drop the timeout-orchestration tests whose subject no longer exists — the live per-phase-budget contract is already pinned in tagging_pipeline_runner_test.dart.

verdict.evidence: TagGenerator.generate() has no production caller: grep of lib/ for `.generate(` finds only List.generate/fingerprint/etc., none on a TagGenerator. TaggingService (lib/services/tagging/tagging_service.dart:36, 283) uses the runner (`generator:` passed to TaggingPipelineRunner) and `generatePhase1Only` — never `generate()`. Live orchestration is TaggingPipelineRunner (lib/services/tagging/tagging_pipeline_runner.dart:122-165): per-phase Future.timeout budgets with continue-past-failed-phase semantics, calling runPhase1..runPhase5 via _defaultPhaseCallables. The dead generate() (lib/services/tagging/tag_generator.dart:165-268) implements different semantics: stopwatch check-after-each-phase, skip-ALL-remaining-on-timeout (HIGH-7 asymmetry documented at lines 160-164). The test file contains 142 `generator.generate(` invocations (finding claimed "250+" — count is overstated but the substance holds), including C3/HIGH-7 timeout-orchestration tests whose subject is unreachable in production. Not covered by accepted-deviations.md (no entry about tagging tests or dead orchestrators).

title: No true end-to-end pipeline test exists for the USP chain (raw recipe text in → tags out); the file named 'Import → Tagging Integration' runs no import and fabricates the ingredient lookup
evidence: test/integration/tagging/import_tagging_integration_test.dart:46-68 — despite the header 'Verifies that recipes imported through various strategies are properly auto-tagged', no import strategy is ever invoked: recipes are built with RecipeBuilder, the ingredient lookup (the component that actually determines allergen correctness) is replaced with a canned `TaggingTestHelper.createMeatLookup()`, and tagging is run through the dead `tagGenerator.generate()` (line 59) rather than the live TaggingService→TaggingPipelineRunner path. This violates 'mock dependencies, not the subject' twice over: the subject (import→lookup→tag join) is mocked away, and the orchestrator exercised is unreachable in production. A regression where TextImportStrategy emits ingredient lines in a format IngredientLookupService can't match (e.g. quantities not stripped) would produce all-UNKNOWN allergen tags in production while every test here stays green.
recommendation: Add one genuine end-to-end test: raw Swedish recipe text → ImportManager.autoImport (real TextImportStrategy) → real TaggingService.generateTags with a real TagGenerator and a real/emulator-backed (or fixture-seeded) IngredientLookupService → assert specific allergen TriStates and tags. Even a single such test covering 3-4 representative recipes closes the largest seam in the pipeline. Rename or rewrite the current file so its name matches what it proves.

verdict.evidence: Read test/integration/tagging/import_tagging_integration_test.dart in full: no import strategy or ImportManager is ever invoked — recipes come from RecipeBuilder (lines 49-54), ingredient lookups are canned helpers (TaggingTestHelper.createMeatLookup(), line 56), and tagging runs via tagGenerator.generate() (line 59). Production path check: lib/services/tagging/tagging_service.dart:34,73-106 shows generateTags() goes through TaggingPipelineRunner, and lib/services/tagging/tagging_pipeline_runner.dart:242,321 explicitly says it *replicates* TagGenerator.generate's behavior rather than calling it — the only live TagGenerator call in lib/ is generatePhase1Only (tagging_service.dart:283), so tagGenerator.generate() is indeed not the production orchestration path (minor nuance: TagGenerator itself is not fully dead, only its generate() entry point). Coverage check for a real e2e elsewhere: test/integration/import/import_end_to_end_test.dart contains no tagging/lookup references at all; the only tests touching TaggingService.generateTags (tagging_service_test.dart:22-23,109) mock IngredientLookupService. No entry in .claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md covers this. So the claimed gap — no test exercises raw text → import strategy → real lookup → live pipeline → tags — is real, and the file's header (lines 1-4) overstates what it proves.

title: Correction capture (the flywheel's intake) only fires for Tier-1 URL imports — photo/OCR, text-paste, social, and URL tiers 2-7 never produce training data
evidence: recipe_persistence_manager.dart:475 returns early unless `savedRecipe.sourceUrl` is non-empty; recipe_form_viewmodel.dart:156-161 only seeds `originalParsedRecipe` by retrieving from ParsedRecipeCache keyed by sourceUrl; and the ONLY writer to ParsedRecipeCache is url_import_strategy.dart:454-457 inside `_convertParsedRecipeToImportResult`, which handles ParseResults from RecipeParserService (Tier 1 / Tier-3 re-run). So photo/OCR imports (PhotoImportStrategy → TextImportStrategy, no ParsedRecipe, no sourceUrl), text-paste, Instagram/TikTok/YouTube pipelines, and URL imports that succeeded via schema.org / site-parser / WebScraper / LLM / user-assisted tiers all bypass RecipeDiffCalculator entirely. Photo/OCR corrections are precisely the highest-value CRF training data (the cookbook-scan use case in project memory), and user-assisted (Tier 7) imports are by definition 100% correction — both are discarded.
recommendation: Widen the capture gate: (a) have every import strategy attach its pre-edit parse snapshot (a ParsedRecipe or the imported Recipe itself) to the form state via SourceArtefact/recipe-id keying instead of sourceUrl-only ParsedRecipeCache lookup; (b) in `_trackParsingCorrectionsInBackground`, drop the sourceUrl guard and diff against that snapshot for any imported recipe, tagging `source` (url/photoOcr/textPaste/instagram) so the retrain export can filter. This one change multiplies the flywheel's intake surface from ~1 of 8 import paths to all of them.

verdict.evidence: All three cited claims check out. (1) recipe_persistence_manager.dart:475-477 — `_trackParsingCorrectionsInBackground` returns early if `savedRecipe.sourceUrl` is null/empty AND if `_state.originalParsedRecipe` is null; both must be present for RecipeDiffCalculator + ParsingCorrectionRepository.save + logParseCorrection fan-out to run. (2) recipe_form_viewmodel.dart:156-167 is the ONLY place `setOriginalParsedRecipe` is set to non-null (grep of lib/: only other setter call is the clear at recipe_persistence_manager.dart:511), and it retrieves from ParsedRecipeCache keyed by `initialRecipe.sourceUrl`. (3) grep of lib/ shows the ONLY `cache.store()` writer is url_import_strategy.dart:454-457 inside `_convertParsedRecipeToImportResult`, which is called solely from `_tryEnhancedParser` (line 221) — i.e. the RecipeParserService path at Tier 1 (line 113-115) and its Tier-3 headless-HTML re-run (lines 132-138), which the finding itself acknowledges. URL Tiers 2/4/5/6/7 (structured extraction line 117-124, scraper fallback 150-155, HTML text parse 160-167, LLM 169-180, user-assisted 182-189) return ImportResults without touching the cache, so their saves produce no correction diff. Photo/text/social pipelines never write the cache either (no ParsedRecipeCache references outside url_import_strategy). The nearby `_editEmitter.emit` (recipe_persistence_manager.dart:453) is only the `post_import_edit` analytics event (recipe_edit_analytics_emitter.dart), not training-data capture, so no other guard covers this. Not listed in accepted-deviations.md.

title: Parse-quality measurement (parse_events) has the same blind spot: photo, text, and social imports emit no parse events, so the dashboard measures only the URL path
evidence: Grep for ParseEventLogger call sites across lib/: only url_import_strategy.dart and recipe_parser_service.dart invoke it (plus model/repo/tracker definitions). PhotoImportStrategy delegates to TextImportStrategy (pure regex, no RecipeParserService), and the Instagram/TikTok/share-sheet paths (ExtractionManager) log nothing structured. TextImportStrategy's zero-ingredient case is an AppLogger.warning (text_import_strategy.dart:450-463), not a queryable event. Result: the admin dashboard's Parsing-detaljer tab and the site_configs success counters see only URL imports; success rate for photo/OCR — a core USP pillar — is unmeasurable in production.
recommendation: Route all terminal import outcomes through ParseEventLogger (it already accepts a `source` field). Cheapest slice: one call at the end of ImportManager._parseWithStrategy with strategy name, success, needsAssistance, and elapsed time — that covers every path in one place instead of per-strategy instrumentation, and reuses the existing logParseEvent CF and dashboard.

verdict.evidence: Grep for ParseEventLogger/logParseEvent across lib/ shows only two invoking sites: lib/services/import/url_import_strategy.dart:36 and lib/services/parsing/recipe_parser_service.dart:166/889 (the rest are model/repo/tracker definitions). RecipeParserService is only referenced from url_import_strategy.dart (lines 37-61), so parse events fire on the URL path alone. photo_import_strategy.dart:62,220 delegates OCR text to TextImportStrategy, which contains no parser-service or event-logger references; its zero-ingredient/zero-instruction outcomes are AppLogger.warning calls at text_import_strategy.dart:452-462 (not queryable events). lib/services/import/pipelines/ (Instagram etc.) has zero ParseEvent/RecipeParserService matches. Not covered by accepted-deviations.md. Net effect matches the finding: photo/text/social import outcomes are invisible to the parse_events dashboard.

title: CRF retrain pipeline's deploy and measure links are broken: no Storage upload for RemoteWeightLoader, hash registry forces an app release anyway, and no eval gate before shipping new weights
evidence: retrain_with_corrections.sh (read in full, 39 lines) ends at Stage 4 writing `assets/data/crf_ingredient_weights.json` and printing 'Run tests' — no upload step, no gsutil/storage reference anywhere in scripts/crf/. RemoteWeightLoader expects `models/crf_ingredient_weights.json` in Firebase Storage (remote_weight_loader.dart:29) and hash-verifies downloads against the compiled-in registry (lines 171-174 → _expected_model_hashes.dart), so a retrained model can only reach users via (a) a manual, undocumented Storage upload PLUS a code change adding the new hash PLUS an app release, or (b) the bundled asset in the next store build. Also: export-corrections.ts:51 reads the client-written `parsing_corrections` aggregate (no server-side PII re-scrub, unlike the _v2 path), and the script has no before/after evaluation against the golden dataset (test/golden/crf_ingredients.json) — a retrain that regresses accuracy would ship silently.
recommendation: Add Stage 5 to the script: run the CRF golden/eval tests against old and new weights and print the precision/recall delta, refusing to proceed on regression; add Stage 6: upload to Storage at the RemoteWeightLoader path, bump the version file, and print the SHA-256 for the hash-registry entry. Document that a hash-registry code change is required (or pre-register the next N version hashes at release time if you want true OTA weight updates). This is 'built but never connected' rather than missing — the loader half already works and is tested.

verdict.evidence: scripts/crf/retrain_with_corrections.sh (full, 39 lines) ends at Stage 4 writing assets/data/crf_ingredient_weights.json and printing "Run tests" — no upload; grep of scripts/ for gsutil/storage/upload finds nothing CRF-related, and scripts/crf/ contains no deploy tooling. lib/services/parsing/crf/remote_weight_loader.dart:30 hard-codes Storage path 'models/crf_ingredient_weights.json' and lines ~171-179 fail-close SHA-256-verify against kExpectedCrfWeightHashes; _expected_model_hashes.dart:10-35 documents the mandatory manual flow (compute hash → add registry entry in a PR → upload → ship client release → bump version file), confirming a retrained model needs an undocumented manual upload + code change + app release, or waits for the next bundled-asset store build. functions/src/admin/export-corrections.ts:51 reads the raw parsing_corrections collection with no server-side PII re-scrub. No eval gate: the pipeline never runs the golden set (test/golden/crf_ingredients.json exists) or compares old vs new weights. Minor nuance only: train_crf.py:402 does evaluate on a held-out split of the merged data and prints metrics, so "no eval" is slightly overstated — but it is informational, not a gate, and not against the golden corpus, so a regression would still ship silently. All load-bearing claims hold; not covered by accepted-deviations.md.

title: Entire global `ingredients` collection is fetched from Firestore per app session, plus an hourly full re-fetch — reads scale as users × sessions × collection size
evidence: firebase_ingredient_repository.dart:153-183 `_doLoadCache()` runs `await _collection.get()` on the whole `ingredients` collection (no limit, no field selection, default server source — every doc is a billed read). :49 sets `cacheTtl = 1 hour`; :107-123 `_ensureCacheLoaded()` triggers a full background re-fetch (`loadCache(forceReload: true)`) once the cache is an hour old, so long sessions pay the full collection repeatedly. The collection is large and growing: the codegen mirror `lib/constants/known_ingredients.dart` is 5,741 lines (~5.6k quoted names), and the collection keeps growing via the Livsmedelsverket sync pipeline and `analyzeCorrections` learned-alias writes. This load fires lazily on the first tagging/import/lookup of every session — i.e. for essentially every active user. At a few thousand docs × a couple of sessions/day, this is the dominant per-user Firestore read cost of the whole pipeline and it grows on two axes at once (user count and ingredient count).
recommendation: Stop serving the read-mostly, admin-managed ingredient DB as N Firestore doc reads. Options in order of preference: (a) publish a version-stamped JSON snapshot to Firebase Storage/CDN (the export-ingredients.ts → JSON pipeline already exists) and have the client read ONE `system/ingredients_version` doc, downloading the snapshot only when the version changed; (b) ship the bundled snapshot in the app (known_ingredients codegen already exists) and only fetch a delta of docs with `updatedAt > bundledVersion`; (c) at minimum, raise cacheTtl from 1h to 24h and gate the refresh on a version doc. Any of these cuts steady-state reads by ~99%.

verdict.evidence: firebase_ingredient_repository.dart confirms every mechanic claimed: line 157 `_doLoadCache()` runs `await _collection.get()` on the whole global `ingredients` collection with no limit/field selection and default (server) source; line 49 `cacheTtl = 1 hour`; lines 115-133 `_ensureCacheLoaded()` serves stale and fires `_refreshCacheInBackground()` → `loadCache(forceReload: true)` once the cache is an hour old, so long sessions do repeated full-collection fetches. `_ensureCacheLoaded()` is awaited at every lookup entry point (lines 259, 268, 432, 450, 457, 467, 526-544...), so the full load fires lazily on first ingredient use per session. Collection scale claim checks out: `lib/constants/known_ingredients.dart` is 5,741 lines (~5.6k names). The class doc comment (lines 13-18) shows this design is intentional as an improvement over a permanent `.snapshots()` listener, but does not mitigate the reads×users×sessions×collection-size scaling. Not listed in `.claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md` (no ingredient entry). Only nuance: docs with unchanged data still bill as full reads on `.get()` from server, so Firestore offline persistence does not reduce cost — the finding's cost math holds. Note it also conflicts with the project's own "Firebase — avoid unnecessary reads" cost principle in CLAUDE.md.
